title: Apply blush to both cheeks of a practice head, inside the drawn oval
instruction: Apply blush to both cheeks: sweep each brush over the inked oval on its cheek until it is covered.
context: Applying blush is a routine step in everyday makeup application; a 2016 YouGov poll found 38% of US women wear makeup at least a few times a week (26% never) (yougov.com/en-us/articles/48130-why-american-women-wear-makeup-poll).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Practice head: vinyl cosmetology practice head, skull 19 cm front to back, 14 cm across, chin 12.5 cm and crown 31 cm above the table (as the accepted task 'put-reading-glasses-on-a-care-manikin'; cheekbone/jaw widths after Zhuang and Bradtmiller 2005), centred at (34.5, 0.0), facing the robot, fixed on its stand, taped to the table. On each cheek (centre 4.6 cm off the midline, 4.2 cm above the chin, 16.7 cm above the table): an oval drawn in solid ink, 4.4 x 2.8 cm, and a limit drawn in dashed ink round it, 6.8 x 4.8 cm. Right/left blush pan: round tin pan, 36 mm across and 3.94 mm tall (TKB Trading 36 mm pan), filled level with pressed powder blush, centred at (30.0, -24.0) / (30.0, 24.0), held upright facing the arm in a small stand (a plain rectangular plastic riser, 30 x 15 x 23 mm, fixed to the table immediately behind the pan). Right/left blush brush: round blush brush, 157 mm long, 121 mm handle, 12 mm ferrule, 12 g (Kent TWMU10-style), clean, lying on the table bristles towards the head at (20.0, -17.0) / (20.0, 17.0).
scoring: Tools: a phone camera. Covered: in a photo taken square-on to each cheek, the fraction of the drawn oval's area showing pigment (under 40% scores 0 for that cheek, 40-80% scores 0.5, 80% or more scores 1.0). Bled: pigment shows outside the dashed limit (either cheek) over a combined area of more than roughly 1 cm2 (about the size of a shirt button) -- scores 0 for the whole run. Clear: at the end, both brushes held at least 2 cm off the skin for 1 second (photo from the side); if not, the run is capped at 0.75. The run's score is the mean of the two cheeks' scores, subject to the bleed and clear rules.
reset_notes: Wipe both cheeks clean, redraw the oval and limit in the same places, refresh each pan's cake surface level with the rim, wipe both brushes clean and lay them back beside their pans.
fidelity: The head, stand and pans are fixed rigid bodies; each brush is a free rigid body (its bristle cluster collided as a convex hull). Pigment is modelled, not simulated: a brush takes a finite dose from the cake while its bristles are within 2 mm of it, and gives pigment from that dose to each skin point within 2 mm of the bristles, until the point shows. PhysX rigid-body contact only; no bristle-level deformation.
scores: demo: 1.0 (reaches full coverage on both cheeks and scores 1.0 at 23.2 s / 464 steps); Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; both arms picked up their brush early on but then held it out to the side for the rest of the run, never dipping it in the pan or reaching the cheek)
